attorneys.name: Dawn Farina
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
With over three decades of trial-tested experience and as a former prosecutor, Dawn Farina has built an extraordinary law practice by utilizing her well-earned expertise and legal knowledge with precise and positive results. She has the unique ability and expertise to identify weaknesses and issues in the prosecution’s case and use that information to her client’s advantage.

By successfully executing thousands of felony and misdemeanor criminal cases during her career, Dawn can provide a first-rate defense for clients facing challenging situations – including charges of aggravated murder, child sexual assault, rape, domestic violence, burglary, theft, driving under the influence, among many more.

Dawn has extensive knowledge in presenting and defending against all types of forensic evidence and asserted defenses, including self-defense, mental disease, cell phone, and DNA.

Upon graduating from law school, Dawn worked as a public defender before being recruited by the Pierce County Prosecutor’s Office. Dawn spent 29 years with the Pierce County Prosecutor’s Office, first as a trial attorney and working up the rank to the position of Chief of Staff. As COS, she worked with three different elected prosecutors during her tenure. In addition to trying some of the biggest felony cases in the county, Dawn oversaw over 200 employees and supervised the office’s top leadership team, including the Chief Criminal Deputy and the Chief Criminal Investigator. Dawn oversaw the management of over 13,000 cases each year.

Dawn left the prosecutor’s office to pursue a new opportunity with the City of Fife. They recruited her to create a new prosecution program in their municipal court system. As the City Prosecutor, Dawn was responsible for the effective execution of all aspects of prosecution for the city. This included conducting jury trials, negotiating plea agreements, reviewing and charging cases, and writing and arguing appeals.

Dawn spent over three decades training and advising law enforcement on police use of force, police pursuits, search warrants, and investigation of crimes. She knows what to look for when reviewing a case investigated by law enforcement and can spot deficiencies in their investigation.

Dawn is the former President of the Tacoma-Pierce County Bar Association, which represents over 1400 lawyers in Pierce County. She is the recipient of the Special Pro-Bono Leadership Award for facilitating the creation of a Native American Legal Aid Program in Pierce County, recipient of the Gold Star Award from the Sexual Assault Crisis Center of Pierce County, recipient of the Fife Police Department’s special recognition award for providing expertise and insight to the Fife Police Department, and recipient of City of Fife’s excellence in public service award.

Puget Law Group welcomed Dawn in 2024 as our Senior Attorney. In 2025, she was named as a Partner in the firm.

Dawn Farina is a dedicated and steadfast advocate for individuals facing criminal charges. She brings a strategic mindset and an exceptional work ethic to every case, ensuring her clients receive the high-quality, effective representation they deserve. Known for achieving outstanding results, Dawn consistently exceeds expectations and delivers both success and hope to those she represents—earning her a reputation as a highly sought-after criminal defense attorney.

attorneys.name: Janay L. Farmer
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration and Citizenship Lawyers in Kent, WA
attorneys.bio:
Janay Farmer is an associate attorney practicing exclusively immigration law, with a focus on complex removal defense, humanitarian processes, and family-based immigration matters. Ms. Farmer practices before the Department of Homeland Security Executive Office of Immigration Review, the Board of Immigration appeals, the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals, USCIS, the Superior Court of Washington, and the Department of State. She is admitted to the bars of Washington State, New York State, and the Eastern District of New York.

Ms. Farmer graduated from the University of Washington School of Law. Following law school, Janay worked as an Assistant Professor of Law at Haramaya University School of Law in Ethiopia. Upon returning to the United States, Janay worked and voluteered at numerous human rights and immigration-focused nonprofit organizations in New York City, including MADRE, Girl Rising, Immigration Equality, and the NYC Housing Court, as well as the HIV Law Project at Housing works, where she provided direct immigration and public benefits representation to low income New Yorkers living with HIV and AIDS.

Ms. Farmer joined Hanis Irvine Prothero in June 2019 as an Associate Immigration attorney. She continues to represent French-speaking asylees Pro Bono for the Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, and is a frequent volunteer with the King County Bar Association immigration clinics and Centro Rendu. Ms. Farmer is fluent in French and conversant in Spanish and American Sign Language.

attorneys.bio:
Paul Ferman was born in Stockholm, Sweden. When he was 9, his family settled in Bremerton, where they have lived since. Paul attended Gonzaga University, where he earned a degree in English Literature. After college, he worked at and eventually managed the Boat Shed Restaurant, a local landmark, while earning a Master's degree in Secondary Education from Old Dominion University. After teaching for a year, Paul moved with his wife to Virginia to attend Law School at George Mason University. Paul graduated with honors, with a concentration in litigation. After practicing for 2 ½ years in Virginia on a variety of cases, Paul moved back home to Bremerton with his wife and children to be closer to family. Following several months of internship, he took an Associate position with Hall & West in September 2015 and became a partner in the firm effective January 2016. He currently practices primarily in Real Property, Wills and Estate Planning, Probate, Business/Corporations, and Contracts under the mentorship of his decades-experienced partner, Larry Hall.

Paul is a board member of Saint Joseph's Mission Fund, a charity that helps the poorest of the poor in India. He is also an avid bridge player and a former state chess champion.

attorneys.name: Sophia R. Ficarrotta
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Everett, WA
attorneys.bio:
Sophia Ficarrotta brings to the Firm her strong commitment to client advocacy. While her current practice includes complex legal issues from property disputes to guardianship and adoption, she also represents clients in education law, domestic violence, employment law, and civil rights and discrimination claims.

Sophia earned her J.D. from Gonzaga University School of Law, where she co-founded the Student Organization for Student Advocacy and served as a student representative on the LGBTQ+ Law Caucus. During law school, she focused on advancing survivors' rights, contributing to amicus curiae briefs for the Washington State Supreme Court on institutional liability for survivors of sexual violence and the United States Supreme Court on Second Amendment protections for survivors of intimate partner terrorism.

Before law school, Sophia graduated from the University of North Carolina at Wilmington with a B.F.A. in Creative Writing and a minor in Anthropology. An internationally published poet, Sophia brings creativity and empathy to her legal practice, bridging advocacy and storytelling to amplify the voices of those she represents.

When Sophia isn't at work, she's curating her Instagram where she and her partner pair wine and cheese with their current reads.

attorneys.name: Stephan O. Fjelstad
attorneys.practice_type: Community Association Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
My practice centers on general counsel, contract drafting and dispute resolution for community association clients. Services include covenants interpretation & enforcement, construction contract drafting, major building repair & rehabilitation project guidance, association governance, and general vendor agreements review and revision.

I have been serving community association clients principally since I joined this law firm in 2007. Immediately prior to joining this firm, I was owner of a law firm practicing commercial and real property litigation, and business advising. Before that I was a full time litigator with the Seattle law firm Tousley Brain Stephens and with the San Francisco firm Carroll, Burdick & McDonough.

I have lectured and presented at Washington State Community Association Institute (WSCAI) educational events and at Continuing Legal Education seminars on various topics such as short-term rentals, view covenants and impairment law, general primers on homeowner association law, architectural design review and enforcement in community associations, non-profit corporation records policies and retention duties, construction contracts, and surface water diversion and lateral support law. I have contributed articles to the WSCAI Journal and other publications, and most recently have served on the WSCAI Task Force on Alternative Dispute Resolution.

For more than fifteen years Brian worked at all levels of the King County Department of Public Defense (DPD). As a staff attorney Brian represented hundreds of clients accused of offenses from simple misdemeanors to the most serious felony offenses. His aggressive motions and trial practice secured acquittals, dismissals, and other favorable outcomes in many cases including homicide, rape, felony assault, vehicular assault, DUI, drug offenses, firearm offenses, violations of no-contact orders, forgery, and motor vehicle theft. Brian then supervised a felony unit, managing an office of eight lawyers, training lawyers new to felony practice, and representing DPD in bench-bar meetings with the presiding judge and other stakeholders. Finally, Brian served in the Director’s Office as Assistant Special Counsel for Policy and Practice. That role involved direct engagement on a wide range of policy issues, from inhumane jail conditions to Covid-era court operations, to the treatment of those with severe mental illness in the criminal legal system. In that position Brian also led or assisted in the drafting of amicus briefs to the Courts of Appeal and Supreme Court on issues including the right to counsel, racially biased policing, conditions of juvenile detention, and other important constitutional issues. In addition, he led DPD’s work in post-conviction representation of individuals sentenced as young adults to extraordinarily long sentences in the 1990s and early 2000s, and has had the privilege of assisting several clients leave prison many years before their original sentences were to expire.

Brian has a deep wealth of knowledge regarding Washington criminal law and procedure. Over the course of his career Brian regularly provided training for DPD staff on both foundational topics and emerging issues in the law. While in the Director’s Office he provided monthly caselaw updates for all DPD staff on developments in the criminal law, analyzing all published Washington appellate cases and discussing their potential application to DPD’s clients. He is particularly interested in search and seizure issues, racial disproportionality, and the culpability of young people and those with other cognitive impairments.

Brian holds an undergraduate degree in Criminal Justice from Northeastern University and attended New York University School of Law, where he was a member of the Law Review.

attorneys.name: Josias Flynn
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation and Business Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
Josias E. Flynn is the founder of Legal Resolutions, a law firm dedicated to providing skilled legal representation in civil litigation, business law, personal injury, and estate disputes. He works closely with individuals and businesses in Pierce and King counties, helping them navigate complex legal challenges with a strategic and client-focused approach.

Mr. Flynn started his legal career at a larger firm in Seattle, where he gained extensive litigation experience handling a broad range of disputes. His background as a "big law firm-trained litigator" allows him to offer his clients the level of skill and knowledge typically associated with larger firms—while providing personalized, client-centered service.

Practice Focus

Business Law & Commercial Litigation

Mr. Flynn represents businesses in contract disputes, commercial litigation, and other business-related legal matters. He understands the operational and financial stakes involved, working proactively to resolve disputes efficiently.

Personal Injury

He helps individuals recover compensation for motor vehicle accidents, premises liability claims, wrongful death, and other personal injury cases. His background as a former defense attorney provides him with unique insight into how opposing parties build their cases.

Estate & Trust Disputes

Mr. Flynn assists clients in wills, trusts, and estate disputes, including contested wills, trust litigation, and conflicts over asset distribution. He works to resolve these sensitive matters with a combination of legal skill and practical guidance.

A Thoughtful Approach to Legal Disputes

Every case is different, and Mr. Flynn prioritizes understanding his clients' unique needs before crafting a strategy. While he is an experienced litigator, he recognizes that litigation can be time-consuming, costly, and emotionally challenging. He explores negotiation, arbitration, and other dispute resolution methods whenever they serve his clients' best interests.

"There’s no one-size-fits-all solution," he explains. "Each case requires a tailored approach to achieve the best outcome—whether that means litigating aggressively or finding an alternative resolution."

At Legal Resolutions, Josias Flynn is committed to delivering strategic, results-driven advocacy. Contact him today to discuss how he can assist with your legal needs.

attorneys.name: Jennifer A. Forquer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer A. Forquer has been with Meridian Family Law since 2011 and has been a partner since 2013. She decided to dedicate her career to family law in 2001 when she joined a boutique, family law firm in Bethesda, Maryland where she eventually became a partner. She returned to Washington 2007 and after a brief hiatus she returned to the practice of family law in 2009.

She has extensive experience in family law and provides a wide range of services. These include representation in complex divorce proceedings, high-asset divorce, child support, same-sex family law issues, co-habitation agreements, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, collaborative divorce, parenting plans, and post-divorce matters such as modification of child support, modification of spousal support (alimony) and the enforcement of court orders and settlement agreements.

She works closely with her clients to ensure they have the information they need to make informed decisions and to plan their path forward. She believes that her clients and their children future is of utmost importance, and that while contested litigation is sometimes necessary or unavoidable, practical advice and out of court solutions can often lead to better, long-term results and can allow people to resolve their family matter with respect. In addition to being an adept litigator, she is collaboratively trained and represents clients in the collaborative divorce process.

Personal

Born and raised in AK, Jennifer enjoys the outdoors whether it be creating and tending to extensive flower gardens, kayaking, or trolling for king salmon in Cook Inlet with her family. She's been married and divorced, but now lives with her significant other (Jeff) and their two adopted and spoiled cats. She and Jeff travel frequently to AK and the east coast to visit family.

attorneys.name: Veronica A Freitas
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Veronica focuses her practice in family law. She routinely handles cases with significant assets which require business and property valuations. She also represents individuals involved in complex child custody disputes, including those with allegations of domestic violence. Veronica frequently represents individuals involved in same-sex relationships with their family law matters.

Veronica has an LLM in taxation which makes her particularly well qualified to evaluate the property and financial aspects of cases. In addition, she litigated several high profile criminal cases and gained invaluable trial experience. Her diverse background compliments her family law practice and her clients benefit from her breadth of knowledge and experience.

Her criminal background is advantageous in many family law matters, especially those where criminal allegations are pending, or domestic violence is alleged and protection orders are being sought. Her tax and estate planning experience is particularly useful when drafting and reviewing pre or post nuptial agreements and property settlement agreements.

Veronica has direct and frequent contact with her clients. She keeps her clients informed and involved in their cases throughout her representation. Her personal philosophy is to attempt to resolve cases as expeditiously as possible so that her clients can move forward with their lives. She is not anxious to go to engage in a court battle, but she is very qualified and competent to do so in those instances where a court appearance or trial is necessary.

attorneys.name: Sharon Friedrich
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law/Child Support/Child Custody/Collaborative/Divorce/Same-Sex Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Behind Sharon Friedrich's graceful, elegant style is a razor-sharp legal mind fortified by more than 20 years of practice experience. This Washington native, who earned her undergraduate degree with honors at Pacific Lutheran University, had been employed in both the public and private law sectors before joining the Meridian Family Law team in 2012. Throughout her impressive legal career, Sharon has remained entirely consistent on one point: her steadfast devotion to family law and the clients she serves.

"Family law entails more than just a legal procedure," she explains. "My clients are facing the unknown and are dealing with multiple changes in their lives. They have to juggle jobs and budgets, face the prospect of moving, take care of their children, and deal with the inevitable stress that results from family conflict. In sum, they are confronting a total disruption in their family lives-today, tomorrow, and into the future." For Sharon, this means a chance to provide sensitive, effective, and client-focused service.

"It's a highly emotional and personal process," adds the Seattle University law graduate who was a member of the school's Client Counseling and Negotiation Board. "Clients are thrown into an arena they do not understand, without the tools they need to protect themselves and their children...That's where I come in."

Sharon excels in complex or difficult divorce, child custody, and parenting law cases. She believes that a well-defined, well-prepared approach to achieving reasonable goals is the best path to satisfaction for her clients. "In order to optimize our position in a case," Sharon says, "it is critical that my clients and I define our goals at the outset and then move forward to achieve them with clarity, decisiveness, and conviction while also maintaining the flexibility necessary to address what is often a fluid and dynamic situation."

sections.content:
Behind Sharon Friedrich's graceful, elegant style is a razor-sharp legal mind fortified by more than 20 years of practice experience. This Washington native, who earned her undergraduate degree with honors at Pacific Lutheran University, had been employed in both the public and private law sectors before joining the Meridian Family Law team in 2012. Throughout her impressive legal career, Sharon has remained entirely consistent on one point: her steadfast devotion to family law and the clients she serves.

"Family law entails more than just a legal procedure," she explains. "My clients are facing the unknown and are dealing with multiple changes in their lives. They have to juggle jobs and budgets, face the prospect of moving, take care of their children, and deal with the inevitable stress that results from family conflict. In sum, they are confronting a total disruption in their family lives-today, tomorrow, and into the future." For Sharon, this means a chance to provide sensitive, effective, and client-focused service.

"It's a highly emotional and personal process," adds the Seattle University law graduate who was a member of the school's Client Counseling and Negotiation Board. "Clients are thrown into an arena they do not understand, without the tools they need to protect themselves and their children...That's where I come in."

Sharon excels in complex or difficult divorce, child custody, and parenting law cases. She believes that a well-defined, well-prepared approach to achieving reasonable goals is the best path to satisfaction for her clients. "In order to optimize our position in a case," Sharon says, "it is critical that my clients and I define our goals at the outset and then move forward to achieve them with clarity, decisiveness, and conviction while also maintaining the flexibility necessary to address what is often a fluid and dynamic situation."

attorneys.name: Bradford J. Fulton
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bellevue, WA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Fulton graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Washington State University in 1985 and from the University of Washington School of Law in 1988.

Brad is admitted to practice by the Washington State Bar Association, Oregon Bar Association (via reciprocity), United State District Courts, Western and Eastern Districts, United States Court of Appeals (Ninth Circuit) and the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Fulton dedicates much time to bettering his profession, having served on the Board of Governors of the Washington State Association for Justice (WSAJ) - formerly the Washington State Trial Lawyers Association (WSTLA) - a 2,600 member volunteer plaintiff's lawyer association, since 1995, and served as the WSAJ President during 2009-2010. Mr. Fulton has also been invited to speak at and/or chair more than 30 Continuing Legal Education seminars on various legal topics, including in the States of Washington, Oregon, New Mexico, Idaho and Quebec, Canada.

Mr. Fulton was also named a "Rising Star" by Washington Law & Politics magazine in both 1999-2000 and 2000-2001, and as a "Super Lawyer" (top 4-5% of lawyers in the State as voted by one's peers) by the same publication each year, 2001 through present. In 2006-2007, Mr. Fulton was also voted by his peers as being among the "Top 40" Washington "Super Lawyers" in the personal injury field.

Brad also received the highest possible rating from Martindale-Hubbell, an "AV" rating in 1998, a rating again based upon evaluations by one's peers, and also carries a 10/10 rating with AVVO.

Mr. Fulton has also served the larger legal community via his involvement in several legal publications, serving as the primary editor of (1) the WSTLA Automobile Accident Litigation Desk book (1999), an 1,800 page, two-volume "How To" manual for the automobile accident lawyer sold throughout Washington and Oregon, and authored or co-authored six (6) separate chapters in the publication, (2) the WSTLA Pleadings and Motions Practice CD-ROM Handbook (2003), a compilation of motions and pleadings used regularly by personal injury and plaintiff's lawyers, which is also sold around the state (and also contributed approximately 40 forms to the same); and (3) the WSAJ Motor Vehicle Collision Litigation Deskbook (2010), an update to the original WSTLA Auto Deskbook. In the latest publications, Mr. Fulton also authored a new chapter on Minor Settlements. Brad also served as editor of the WSTLA/WSAJ Trial News, WSAJ's monthly publication which goes out to all WSAJ members, judges around the state and to many legislators, and has had more than 40 articles published in this state-wide publication.

Finally, Brad is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, an organization whose membership is limited to lawyers who have secured $1,000,000(+) results for their clients.

Brad resides in Seattle with his wife, Danielle, and two children, Hunter and Lauren.

In his spare time, Brad enjoys volunteering on behalf of WSAJ, playing golf, attending Seattle Mariners games and other sporting events, playing recreational softball, participating in fantasy football, hunting and actively participating in the lives of his children.

attorneys.name: Carrie J. Fulton
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
Carrie Fulton Brown, our Managing Attorney at Vindicate, is one of the best criminal defense attorneys in Western Washington. Her skill set is unlike most when it comes to trial advocacy. Of course, trial preparation and discovery are important, but those things can be taught. One element to a lawyer that is not always teachable is the talent and expertise that takes place in a courtroom during trial. Ms. Fulton-Brown’s natural instincts are addicting to watch during trial – juries pay attention, trust what she is saying, and she thrives under pressure.

Ms. Fulton-Brown takes full advantage of the law and tactfully applies it to her defense practices for her clients. She has secured numerous acquittals at trial and not guilty verdicts for her clients. Putting it frankly, she has nearly a decade of obtaining amazing results for her clients.

“Criminal charges are high-stakes and emotional. Allegations have a devastating impact on the accused if not handled correctly.” says Ms. Fulton-Brown. She believes that every client should have a complete understanding of their rights and as an attorney, she makes it her responsibility to provide all her clients with a road map to getting their life back.

attorneys.name: C. Steven Fury
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bellevue, WA
attorneys.bio:
Steven grew up as the son of a logger outside a small town in Washington State. He received his B.A. degree from Stanford University in 1974 and his law degree from Harvard Law School in 1979. Before beginning his practice, he clerked for the Chief Judge of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas.

Steven is one of the founders of Justice Advocacy Africa (JAA), a US non-profit that has since 2003 presented scores of trial advocacy training programs in Uganda, Kenya, Malawi, and Botswana training hundreds of advocates in each country. He has also taught at trial advocacy programs with the General Counsel of the Bar of South Africa. In addition, Steve has presented at many continuing legal education seminars for attorneys, has taught trial advocacy with National Institute for Trial Advocacy, at the University of Washington and Emory schools of law, and in China.

Steven has been selected for “The Best Lawyers in America” since 1995 and Washington State’s Super Lawyers since 2003. In 2012, the Washington State Association for Justice presented its Pillar of Justice award to Steven for the work of JAA in Africa.

attorneys.name: Kate Gagutlova
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
I’ve always believed that every challenge has a solution. My own journey—defined by grit, adaptability, and persistence—has proven that belief time and again. My years in customer service instilled in me a strong commitment to client care, and I carry that forward in every case. I believe every client deserves not only skillful legal representation, but also compassion and unwavering advocacy.

Kate immigrated to the U.S. from Russia at 21 with just $300 after graduating magna cum laude with a master’s degree in linguistics and interpreting. While working various jobs to support herself, she earned a bachelor’s degree in Business and Innovation in Technology from the University of Washington, graduating with highest honors.

Her passion for justice took root at Seattle University School of Law, where she assisted in international law research and represented juvenile clients through the Defenders Clinic. These experiences deepened her commitment to advocacy and revealed the critical need for compassion in the legal system.

Fluent in Russian, English, and French—and proficient in several other languages—Kate connects easily with clients from diverse backgrounds. She personally navigated the U.S. naturalization process, giving her a firsthand understanding of the legal challenges many clients face.

attorneys.name: Brien Galbraith
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Having practiced family law in King County since graduating from law school, Brien has achieved a remarkable depth of experience in advising and representing clients in all family law matters including divorce, contested custody, child support modifications, protection orders, and parentage cases.

Brien believes communication is the key to successful representation. He works with each client individually to form a plan of action for the client's unique set of circumstances. With this approach, he is able to identify with his clients and give them a voice. After determining if it will be possible to reach an amicable resolution or whether litigation or mediation will be necessary, Brien works with the client to execute their plan.

Brien has earned his litigation experience in private family law practice as well as with the San Francisco Division of Child Support as an intern. He also earned a Certificate for Specialization in Litigation while completing his law degree at Golden Gate University School of Law.

Brien is known for his honesty, close relationships with clients, and tenacity in his work on their behalf.

Brien is a Pacific Northwest native; he grew up in Bellevue, Washington and currently resides in Seattle with his wife and young son. He enjoys travelling, karaoke, is a car enthusiast, and a Husky Football Season Ticket holder.

attorneys.name: Shane P. Gale
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Shane joins Dellino Family Law Group having practiced law since 2009. Licensed in four states, he has seen just about everything that can happen in court and will assist you during your time of need as both a zealous advocate and reliable counsel. His goal is to obtain the best possible outcome for you and your family.

Why Family Law

As a divorced dad of three wonderful children, whom I adore, I understand the strain that family conflict can have on children. With that in mind, I aim for resolutions that are long-lasting and reduce the likelihood of future conflict between parents. I grew up in Wisconsin and attended Marquette University for both undergraduate and law school. With a background in finance and litigation experience in the financial sector, I understand the importance of fair and just asset allocation in matters affecting the family, to ensure both stability for you and your children and security as you embark on a new chapter.

About Me

When I am not at work, I enjoy reading, kayaking, traveling, and building and painting my Warhammer 40K models (even if it’s at a glacial pace). I attended Marquette during the era of Dwyane Wade, Wesley Matthews, and Jimmy Butler. Accordingly, I am a die-hard MU basketball fan. Of course, as is required for all Wisconsin natives, I root for the Packers and enjoy attending games as often as possible. Now that you know a little about me, I look forward to hearing more about you.

attorneys.name: Laura Gano
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fircrest, WA
attorneys.bio:
Laura Gano is a dedicated family law attorney, providing compassionate guidance and strategic legal solutions to clients in King, Kitsap, Jefferson, and Snohomish counties. She specializes in handling complex legal issues, conducting in-depth research, and advocating for clients through life’s most challenging transitions.

With a client-centered approach, Laura assists individuals and families with prenuptial agreements, divorces, custody disputes, property matters involving unmarried couples (CIR), post-divorce modifications, and other family law concerns. She strives to make the legal process as clear and stress-free as possible, tailoring her counsel to each client’s unique needs. Laura’s practice philosophy is best captured by a quote from author C.S. Lewis: "You can't go back and change the beginning, but you can start where you are and change the ending."

Outside of her legal practice, Laura enjoys exploring the breathtaking landscapes of the Olympic Peninsula, spending time with her three grown children whenever possible, and giving back to the community through her volunteer work with Kitsap Legal Services.

attorneys.name: Joanna Garza
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Kent, WA
attorneys.bio:
Joanna I. Garza is an associate attorney practicing exclusively in the area of immigration law at Hanis Irvine Prothero, PLLC. Joanna represents clients in a wide variety of immigration-related cases, including family-based immigration matters, U-visas, T-visas, VAWAs, waiver applications, removal defense, and much more.

Joanna was born in Texas and raised in Eastern Washington in a migrant farm working community where she developed her passion for immigrant rights and serving underrepresented communities. Joanna obtained her B.A. from the University of Washington in Seattle and interned at the Mexican Consulate during her undergraduate. After graduating from college Joanna became a Deputy Clerk for Grant County Superior Court.

Joanna received her Juris Doctor Degree from the University of Idaho College of Law in 2018. During law school, she served as the President of the Latino(a) Law Caucus, and Executive Editor and Symposium Editor of the Idaho Critical Legal Studies Journal. Joanna worked as a Northwest Immigrant Rights Project Intern, visiting detained individuals, providing Know-Your-Rights Presentations, hosting on Radio KNDA, and providing direct representation. During this time, she also helped organize and lead a Pro Bono initiative with lawyers across Washington state for farm workers in Othello, Washington.

After graduating from law school, Joanna moved into private practice, focusing exclusively in immigration law. She joined Hanis Irvine Prothero in January of 2020, as a law clerk and then as an immigration attorney. She is an active member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA). Joanna is a native Spanish speaker.

attorneys.name: Carl Joseph Gaul III
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support Lawyers in Everett, WA
attorneys.bio:
Carl listens to his clients. He knows how important each case is to that client. Good results come from hard work. Carl takes the time to explain the law to his clients so they know their rights and the process.

Carl’s work is to represent people. After spending five years in criminal prosecution, Carl has spent over 30 years helping individuals in some of their most important relationships, and some of their most important problems. These are Family Law and Criminal Defense.

For more than three decades Carl has represented people in their family law cases. Family law is much more than divorces. In addition, Carl has won many cases where he represented fathers seeking primary care of their children. Carl represents third-party nonparents seeking custody of children. Carl has won property divisions awarding his client significantly more than half the community property. Family law includes determining parentage, establishing parenting plans and assuring fair child support. Carl has litigated these claims successfully and has mediated many favorable settlements.

When criminal difficulties arise, Carl can help. As a prosecutor he learned criminal law and procedure. In private practice he has used that knowledge to help his clients defend allegations of criminal misconduct. The most frequent involve assaults and alcohol. Carl applies his history of successful litigation to solve these cases.

attorneys.name: Meredith Gerhart
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Olympia, WA
attorneys.bio:
Admitted to the bar in 2010, Meredith Gerhart has devoted her legal career to various facets of family law, specializing in divorce, legal separation, parenting plan modifications, child support adjustments, paternity matters, and relocations.

Apart from her private practice, Meredith serves as a Guardian ad Litem on the Thurston County Title 26 Guardian ad Litem registry. Court appointments frequently task her with advocating for young individuals in dependency proceedings initiated by the State of Washington.

Unlike many of her peers, Meredith pursued law school with a distinct aim of becoming a family law practitioner. Her motivation lies in a steadfast commitment to minimizing potential harm to children involved in court proceedings, whether directly or indirectly. On a daily basis, she actively engages in child-centered and trauma-focused representation, striving to protect the well-being of the most vulnerable members of the community.

Meredith's academic journey comprises achieving a cum laude Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics from Vanderbilt University, followed by earning her J.D. from Gonzaga University School of Law. During her time at Gonzaga, she distinguished herself as the Staff Editor of the Gonzaga Law Review.

attorneys.name: Callie Getty
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Callie Getty is a Senior Attorney at Dellino Family Law Group. Callie’s practice focuses on family and domestic relations matters, including divorce, parenting plan and child support issues, as well as post-decree matters such as modifications.

Callie embodies the perfect combination of experience, compassion, and strong advocacy. Prior to joining Dellino Family Law Group, Callie was a partner at another local family law firm. As a Senior Attorney at DLG, there is not a situation she has not seen and cannot tackle. Whether she is advocating for a client in trial for a high conflict case or negotiating a smart settlement in mediation, her clients know she keeps their best interests at the forefront of her strategy. Her compassionate yet no-nonsense approach makes her who you want on your side when what matters most to you is at stake.

My Approach

My interest in family law comes from my upbringing in a large, blended family. This has led to the firm belief that while a divorce or separation may be the hardest time in a person’s life, a strong, compassionate advocate who will be steadfast in their representation can make all the difference. I strive to be that advocate for each and every one of my clients.

Background

As a native Northwesterner, I grew up in the Seattle-area before heading slightly south to the University of Oregon to obtain my undergraduate degree. I returned to Seattle to attend Seattle University School of Law, and graduated in 2015.

Outside of the office, I enjoy spending time with my family, especially outdoors. In the winter, I like to spend weekends at Crystal Mountain with my husband and three children (two human boys & one 90 lb. doodle). And in the summer, I love soaking up Vitamin D wherever and whenever possible to store for the long NW winters.

attorneys.name: William A. Gilbert
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Moses Lake, WA
attorneys.bio:
William A. (Bill) Gilbert is a trial lawyer whose practice focus is serious personal injury, wrongful death, professional negligence, product liability, employment law and civil rights litigation. Mr. Gilbert has litigated complex cases across the United States, Canada and Central and South America. His litigation achievements include a $716 million jury verdict in a wrongful death action involving the illegal sale of alcohol to minors.

Bill has a unique prospective of the law, borne out of extensive life experience. Prior to becoming an attorney, Bill served in the military, worked on large cattle ranches in his home state of Montana, guided hunters and fisherman in Montana and Alaska, skied professionally, supervised crews on construction projects and spent four years serving the community as a deputy sheriff. Bill has traveled the world extensively following his dreams and passion, exploring, socializing, fishing, hunting and trekking in some of the most remote places on the planet. Bill has experienced the joy of parenthood and high of personal and professional success, as well as the daunting lows of personal tragedy and emotional and financial hardship. His diverse background and wealth of life experience give him a unique prospective on the law and its application to clients' problems. This diversity has proven to be invaluable to the lawyers he works with and the clients he represents.

In addition to being nominated by his peers as a Super Lawyer and listed as one of Top Attorneys in Washington through "Seattle Met," Bill has been selected by his peers as one of the Top Lawyers in Spokane, and named as a Top 100 Lawyer in America. Bill has also earned the distinction of being lead counsel in a verdict award recognized as one of the Nations Top 100 Verdicts through The National Law Journal. Additionally, in recognition of his professional excellence and commitment to his clients, Bill has been inducted into the Worldwide Registry. Bill is also a faculty member of the Gerry Spence Trial Lawyers College where he teaches trial skills to fellow trial lawyers.

Mr. Gilbert provides legal services to clients needing representation in serious personal injury and wrongful death cases, motor vehicle accidents, plane crash injuries, injuries and damages related to defective products, medical negligence, civil rights and employment law.

attorneys.name: Gregory L. Girard
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Kent, WA
attorneys.bio:
Gregory L. Girard’s practice is committed to the aggressive defense of persons accused of a wide array of crimes. Because of his experience and expertise, Greg is one of few criminal defense attorneys who can defend persons accused of the simplest misdemeanor or D.U.I. to the most complicated felony. Greg also represents persons on appeal from criminal convictions or Department of Licensing suspensions in all levels of appellate courts in Washington.

In addition to his practice, Greg has presented and taught on various topics at continuing legal education seminars. Among the subjects he has presented on are The Law of Search and Seizure; Admissibility of Statements Made by the Accused; the Accused’s Right to a Speedy Trial; and the Art of Negotiation in Criminal Defense. Greg is a member of the Washington Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (WACDL), the Washington Defender Association, and the King and South King County Bar Associations.

In 2006 Greg and his partner, Mark Prothero, were named Trial Lawyers of the Year by Presumed Innocent magazine.

During his second year of law school, Greg began working for the Eastside Defenders Association (EDA), where he continued to work as a trial attorney in the juvenile and superior court felony units following his graduation. This began Greg’s commitment to criminal defense in King County that has continued over the last 33 years.

Greg joined Hanis Irvine Prothero in May, 2004, where he continues to provide quality criminal defense. As a partner in Hanis Irvine Prothero, Greg is involved in governing the operations of the firm.

In his spare time, Greg enjoys spending time with his wife Polly, traveling, playing golf, and skiing. In addition, Greg likes reading and spending time in his garden. Greg is also an accomplished Thai chef.

In her first years of practice, Ms. Glenn focused primarily on business litigation, personal injury, employment discrimination, sexual harassment, and advocacy for child crime victims, before turning to family law. She is a determined and compassionate advocate and has a passion for helping her clients navigate the legal system.

Ms. Glenn obtained a B.A. in Political Science and Communications from the University of Washington where she focused on political rhetoric, persuasion, and mass media. She went on to receive her Juris Doctor from Seattle University School of Law and became licensed to practice in the state of Washington in 2018.

In her free time, Ms. Glenn enjoys the outdoors, identifying bird species, teaching her dog new tricks, and spending time with family.

attorneys.name: Jeremy David Goodman
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Criminal Defense | DUI Defense | Protection Orders

Serving Clients throughout Washington state for over a decade.

I believe every person deserves to be heard, protected, and powerfully represented. For over a decade, I have defended individuals across Western Washington facing criminal charges, DUI arrests, and protection order proceedings. My practice is built on trial experience, strategic advocacy, and a deep respect for the people I represent.

I understand what it means to stand up for someone when they feel like the system is stacked against them. Whether you’ve been charged with a crime, pulled over for DUI, or served with a protection order, I will fight for you with focus, compassion, and unshakable resolve. You may feel alone right now, but once I am on your side we will be in this together.

Washington Roots. Defense-Focused from the Start.

I moved to Washington in 2006 to attend the University of Washington. I fell in love with the area and made Washington my home. After earning my undergraduate degree, I graduated from Seattle University School of Law. I concentrated on criminal defense and trial practice. From the beginning, I knew I wanted to be in the courtroom fighting against the power of the Government.

I worked at one our state’s most recognized DUI defense firms for eight years and handled cases in courtrooms all throughout Washington. My experiences gave me an insider’s understanding of how prosecutors think, how to spot weaknesses in the state’s case, and how to prepare for trial with precision.

Proven Results in High-Stakes Cases

I bring a trial-ready approach to every case I take. Whether it’s a misdemeanor or a felony, I prepare thoroughly and strategically from day one. My jury trial record includes:

Not guilty on all 7 charges in a felony jury trial.

A winning record on DUI cases, which includes multiple Not guilty verdicts on cases with breath test result more than double the legal limit.

These outcomes are not accidents. They are the result of hard work, deep legal knowledge, and relentless preparation. I never forget what is truly at stake: my client’s freedom. While negotiating an agreement may sometimes be the safest approach, I am not afraid to take your case all the way to trial to achieve the outcome you deserve.

Clear Counsel. Strategic Defense.

The legal process can feel overwhelming, especially when you’re facing serious consequences. I make it a priority to ensure my clients understand the details of that is happening and feel empowered every step of the way. I take time to answer questions, explain strategy, and build trust. Every case is different, but I approach them all with the same principles: respect, honesty, and determination.

My practice areas include:

Criminal Defense: simple misdemeanors, gross misdemeanors, and felonies

DUI Defense: fighting to invalidate breath tests, finding way to make refusals of breath tests work in my client’s favor, and taking cases all the way through complex trial litigation

Protection Orders: Domestic Violence Protection Orders (DVPO), Anti-Harassment Orders, Sexual Assault Protection Orders, and other civil restraining orders

Local Knowledge. Full-Region Representation.

I serve clients throughout Washington, including King, Snohomish, Pierce, Kitsap, Thurston, Skagit and surrounding counties. I’ve built strong relationships with local courts and understand the unique procedures and personalities that shape each jurisdiction.

Reach out today to schedule a free and confidential consultation. Your defense starts here.

attorneys.name: Gregg T Gottgetreu
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Redmond, WA
attorneys.bio:
Gregg T. Gottgetreu is Herrig & Vogt, LLP's senior construction analyst. He received his Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Wisconsin Madison in 1971. After graduation, he worked for 15 years at Chicago Bridge & Iron Company, an international engineering and construction contractor involved in the municipal, energy, petroleum, and petrochemical industries.

Mr. Gottgetreu's work experience with Chicago Bridge & Iron Company and its affiliates throughout the United States includes nine years as a contracting engineer and project manager, two years as a project planner, two years as a general foreman, an inspector, a welder, a machinist, a draftsman and a design engineer. He has been responsible for constructing planning, estimating, negotiation, and administration of many large and complex projects including a hydroelectric generating station in Yuma, Arizona, a radioactive materials examination facility in Hanford, Washington, an alumina import terminal in Portland, Oregon, structural work at Washington Power Supply System Nuclear Plants 3 and 5 in southwest Washington State, and structures for municipal storage and wastewater treatment plan expansions throughout the mid-western United States.

To effectively manage these multi-disciplined projects, Mr. Gottgetreu specialized in subcontractor bid packaging, evaluation, and coordination, as well as prime contract negotiation, administration, and settlement of change orders, claims, termination, scheduling, and delay issues. Through repeated reviews and negotiations, he has become very familiar with most contracting formats and procedures, both public and private.

Mr. Gottgetreu's training and expertise provides Herrig & Vogt, LLP with the ability to analyze and address the technical and administrative aspects of construction contracts, claims, and disputes in a cost and time-effective manner. Since 1987, Mr. Gottgetreu has prepared, analyzed, evaluated, or defended dispute positions and issues for hundreds of construction matters.

In addition to his work as a construction analyst, Mr. Gottgetreu speaks frequently at seminars concerning construction contract administration and risk control, as well as critical path scheduling. He works out of the Redmond, Washington office of Herrig & Vogt, LLP.

EXPERT WITNESS/CONSULTANT EXPERIENCE

Port of Seattle, Washington Pursuit of claim for recovery from architect for extra costs paid to a contractor on the Seattle Tacoma Airport Concourse D terminal expansion.

City of Pasco, Washington Analysis and defense of contractor's claim for extra costs constructing a sewer line and reconstructing a street.

City of Edmonds, Washington Analysis and defense of contractor's claims for extra costs and delays incurred building a new city hall, police facility, and fire station complex.

City of Redmond, Washington Analysis and defense of contractor's claims for added costs and delay damages incurred widening and reconstructing a parkway.

Active Construction/City of Lacey, Washington, Ruddell Road Reconstruction Preparation and presentation of contractor's claims for extra costs and a schedule analysis demonstrating delays.

RP Richards/Vandenburg, AFB Youth Center Preparation of general contractor's claims for extra costs and a schedule analysis demonstrating delays and corresponding monetary damages.

RP Richards/NASA Building 200 Renovation, Moffett Field, California Preparation of general contractor's claims for extra costs and delays to the completion schedule.

Aetna Insurance/Nevada Geothermal Plant Analysis of contractor's damages incurred after fire destroyed a cooling tower.

Aetna Insurance/Amador, California Hospital Preparation of specialty subcontractor's claims for extra costs incurred because of flooring installation failure.

St. Paul Travelers Surety/City of Phoenix Wastewater Treatment Plant Prepare claim of electrical contractor for contract performance period extension.

St. Paul Travelers Surety/Plateau Electrical Provide rebuttal analysis to general contractor's claims of delayed performance and loss of labor efficiency constructing a wastewater plant.

Viola Constructors/City of Westlake Village, California Prepare contractor's claims for extra work and delays to City Hall/Library/Meeting Rooms Complex.

Acoustech/Thousand Oaks, California, Surgical Hospital Preparation of subcontractor's claims for extra costs and schedule delays.

City of Tolleson, Arizona Evaluate delay claims of a general contractor expanding the capacity of a wastewater treatment plant and defend the City against those claims.

CH2M-HILL Constructors/City of Stockton, California, Wastewater Treatment Plant Defend delay and extra work claims presented by civil work subcontractor.

Lloyds of London Insurance Consortium/Elmendorf AFB Alaska Analysis of costs and expenses

incurred completing remedial efforts on two military hangars.

attorneys.name: Alison Greene
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Vancouver, WA
attorneys.bio:
Alison joined Weber Gunn, PLLC in 1992. Alison worked exclusively under Ken Weber's guidance for several years. In 2001, Alison became a member with the firm and currently serves as President.

Alison graduated from Marymount High School, Los Angeles, California in 1980, Southern Methodist University, Dallas, Texas in 1984 and Northwestern School of Law at Lewis and Clark College, Portland, Oregon in 1988. During 1986 and 1987, Alison had the unique experience of summer European law studies in Scotland, Austria and Hungary.

Alison is a member of the Clark County Bar Association. She has been a Trustee, Secretary, Vice President and President for the Clark County Bar Association. She is a member of the Washington State Bar Association. Long ago, she was a Trustee for the Washington Young Lawyers Division of the Washington State Bar Association and an officer of Clark County Young Lawyers. She serves as a Clark County Superior Court Pro Tem Commissioner presiding over family law and juvenile matters.

As a way of giving back to the community, Alison donates time as a volunteer lawyer through the Clark County Volunteer Lawyers Program.

Outside of the office, Alison enjoys scuba diving, photography and traveling. Traveling is her main interest. Some of her travels have been to China, Italy, Scotland, England, Greece, Turkey, Hungary, Austria, Switzerland, Germany, France, Costa Rica, Panama, Venezuela, Eastern and Western Caribbean, Trinidad, Tobago, Jamaica, Mexico, Canada, India and domestic travels.

Alison is a team member for OWLS Dragonflies, a competitive Northwest dragon boat paddling team whose members are all in the legal community.

Alison has three beautiful children - the four - legged type. They are Sushi, a Shih Tzu; Sassy, a Pug; and the newest addition to the family, Pookie, a Shiht Poo.

attorneys.name: Jessa Greene
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Everett, WA
attorneys.bio:
Jessa is deeply passionate about providing clients with high-quality service, understanding, and care. She approaches every case with the belief that everyone deserves to be treated with compassion, and that their legal strategy should be a direct reflection of their individual desires and needs.

Her professional background is dedicated to serving vulnerable communities, including immigrant communities, domestic violence survivors, and families navigating DHS/CPS intervention.

With a minor in psychology focused on child development and the intersection of trauma and the legal system, Jessa is a strong proponent of collaborative divorce processes whenever possible. She believes in supporting the psychological well-being of children and families through conflict. Her primary goal is to help clients feel empowered during negotiations and mediations, enabling them to make informed decisions and fight for what is right for their family.

Originally from Southern California, Jessa found her true home in the Pacific Northwest after moving here for college. In her free time, you can find her enjoying the rainy weather, and always with a hot cup of tea nearby.

Fun Fact: Jessa has been a dedicated Lego collector since the early 2000s (back when all minifigs were bright yellow!), and she uses major milestones like passing the bar as a reason to acquire elaborate new sets. Her favorites, including the Van Gogh, Botanicals, and Harry Potter kits, are now illuminated with custom lighting kits, and she’s always ready to talk about the latest releases!

attorneys.name: Zachary Knox Griefen
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental and Land Use Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Zachary Knox Griefen has over fifteen years of litigation experience in the fields of environmental and land use law. He has represented environmental organizations, citizen groups, and individuals in cases before municipal boards, state agencies, and state and federal courts. Mr. Griefen has assisted citizen groups and individual clients in halting inappropriate development and enforced federal environmental laws on behalf of environmental organizations and their members. Zak has presented on many legal education panels, on topics including citizen suit litigation, municipal separate storm sewer system regulations, and the regulation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

Prior to joining Bricklin & Newman LLP as an associate, Mr. Griefen was a senior litigator for Conservation Law Foundation, with a focus on civil litigation under the federal Clean Water Act. Prior to joining CLF, Zak worked as a litigation attorney at Cheney, Brock & Saudek, P.C. and clerked at the Vermont Environmental Court.

Zak Griefen has a long-term passion for environmental protection. Zak is an avid angler who ties his own flies and is an enthusiastic user of our public lands and waters.

attorneys.name: Bridget T. Grotz
attorneys.practice_type: Personal injury Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
Bridget Grotz is an empathetic attorney dedicated to justice and helping those who have been harmed emotionally and physically. Her practice focuses on advocating for survivors of childhood sexual abuse. Prior to joining PCVA, Bridget began her legal career as a judicial law clerk for the Honorable Jill Johanson and the Honorable Anne Cruser at the Washington State Court of Appeals, Division II.

Bridget grew up in Burien, Washington and attended the University of California, Berkeley for her undergraduate degree. After graduating with distinction, Bridget served in the Peace Corps teaching primary school literacy and English in Samoa. She then attended the University of Washington School of Law where she was a Senior Managing Editor of the Washington International Law Journal. While in law school, Bridget was actively involved in the Innocence Project Northwest Clinic and the Regulatory Environmental Law and Policy Clinic. She continued to develop her legal skills and champion for important causes while interning at Human Rights Watch, the Environmental Law Institute, and the Washington Appellate Project.

attorneys.name: Gabriela Gutierrez
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Gabriela “Gabi” Gutierrez is an Associate Attorney at Dellino Family Law Group. A fierce advocate for her clients, Gabi recognizes the turmoil that a family law case can cause, leading her clients through the process with dedication, knowledge, and unwavering support.

My Approach

While I am competitive, zealous, and confident, I am also empathetic, professional, and kind. I balance my analytical thinking with a people-centered approach, ensuring that my legal strategies are tailored to each client’s needs. It is easy to work hard for your clients when you are standing up for what is right.

Background

Gabi grew up with a single mom until the age of 9. She knows first-hand what it’s like for children to experience divorce, and what it’s like when your parents enter new relationships and blend their families together. Now, part of a blended family of seven, Gabi understands that family can take on many different forms.

A Southern California native, Gabi moved to Washington in 2015. Eager to enter the work force, Gabi graduated early at the University of Washington for both her undergraduate and law degree, entering the legal world at the age of 24. Before transitioning to family law, Gabi worked in criminal law as both a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney and Public Defender, in Pierce and King County, primarily handling dependency, mental health, and domestic violence-based cases.

About Me

When Gabi is not hard at work on your case, you can find her teaching Pilates, playing with her two longhaired dachshunds, or spending time with her friends and family.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
Bryon grew up in Pierce County and returned after graduating from his undergrad in Idaho and law school in Michigan. He’s thrilled to raise his children here and is proud to provide excellent representation to his clients in the Pacific Northwest. He strives to know each client’s individual case to help them with the best possible outcome during the turmoil that often accompanies most family law cases, confirmed by his client reviews and lawyer endorsements through Avvo.

Bryon’s practice focuses on all aspects of family law. His practice has included uncontested and contested divorces, child custody, child support, domestic disputes, adoptions, and much more. He has received collaborative and mediation training and uses these skills in his practice and to benefit his client. He also provides mediation services and enjoys helping parties resolve disputes outside of the courtroom – contact the office to find out more about his mediation services and to schedule mediation.

Bryon strives to be active with his local and legal community, which helps him stay current in his practice. He is actively involved in professional organizations, including the Family Law Section of the Tacoma-Pierce County Bar Association where he previously served as the Secretary/Treasurer.

When he is not working with his clients, Bryon enjoys spending time with his wife, Lindsey, and their two children, visiting museums, parks, and farmer’s markets and discovering new places to go. He is also active in the community, where he enjoys spending time with his friends and extended family.

attorneys.name: Paige D. Haley
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Paige D. Haley handles divorce, child custody, child support, and related matters. She takes pride in offering sound, realistic advice so her clients enjoy the best possible outcomes. When court action is needed, Paige offers a strong, vigorous presence in court, backed by a depth of knowledge and experience.

In a recent, complex case, a mother with primary custody of the parties’ child sought to relocate to another county in bad faith. Paige won primary custody for her client – after a yearlong battle – while objecting to the relocation. The client calls Paige “dynamic in court”, praises her perseverance and determination, and thanks her for everything.

Paige says she was prepared from childhood to practice family law. She was adopted at birth and her mother remarried twice, giving Paige two stepfathers. “I don’t view my history as negative,” she says. “My family is very close, and I’ve experienced many of the situations my clients have experienced. Sometimes clients feel shame about what they are going through. I tell them, ‘I’ve not only heard it before – I’ve lived it.’”

Paige chose family law because it reaches people on such a personal level. “This is about people’s lives,” she says simply.

attorneys.name: Jeff Hamilton J.D., M.B.A.
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Jeff Hamilton PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
With a unique blend of legal expertise, business acumen, and emotional intelligence, Jeff Hamilton offers a personalized, thoughtful approach to guiding clients through the complexities of business law. Drawing on his background in psychology, Jeff prioritizes understanding his clients' perspectives, creating a safe, confidential, and welcoming space for them to discuss their legal and business challenges openly.

Jeff holds a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Wayne State University (with a minor in German), a Juris Doctorate from Seattle University School of Law, and a Master of Business Administration from the Albers School of Business and Economics. This diverse academic foundation allows him to seamlessly balance legal and business considerations, whether reviewing case briefs, analyzing balance sheets, drafting legal memos, or developing business plans.

Jeff is deeply passionate about the privilege of helping businesses grow and thrive. He works diligently to support clients through every phase of their business journey—from early-stage formation to growth and succession planning. He is committed to providing clear, actionable legal advice that aligns with each client's long-term goals. Jeff is also a staunch advocate for consumer rights and strives to foster respectful and honest engagement between businesses and consumers.

Outside of law, Jeff is a passionate gardener who specializes in growing a variety of sweet and spicy peppers, an aspiring bonsai tree enthusiast, and a comic book aficionado. He’s also a proud dog dad to Clara, a Maltese with a big attitude, who serves as his legal assistant, lap warmer, and squirrel monitor.

Whether you're a startup seeking legal guidance, a business owner planning for the future, or a consumer navigating business interactions, Jeff offers a compassionate, strategic, and highly skilled approach to every client relationship.

attorneys.name: Nicole C.B. Hancock
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Corporate Law Lawyers in Tacoma, WA
attorneys.bio:
Nicole’s practice focuses on estate planning, probate, administration of trusts and estates, and guardianship. Planning for death or declining health can be overwhelming for many. Nicole reduces stress by creating a thoughtful and comprehensive estate plan with the necessary tools to fulfill the client’s wishes that protect and prepare the clients and their families for life’s changes. In order to establish estate plans unique to each client’s needs, Nicole meets with the client to get to know the person, understand their family dynamics, and their desired outcomes. This may include a combination of wills, trusts, powers of attorney, business succession planning, and more.

Nicole helps families navigate the steps of estate administration by advising executors, trustees, attorneys-in-fact, guardians, and conservators to handle their duties and responsibilities. Many clients seek guidance on both simple and complex matters, including possible disputes, transfer of assets, complex relationships, and the payment of debts and expenses.

Nicole also serves as a professional personal representative for estates appointed by the court or by clients who do not have a family member or loved one to serve. Aging can be a challenge. Nicole helps families navigate the cumbersome and complex guardianship and conservatorship process when a loved one is unable to meet health, safety, and financial needs. This may include appointment by the court, meeting periodic reporting requirements, management of assets, and fulfilling duties and responsibilities to the individual. In addition to guardianship work for her clients, Nicole is a Pierce County Superior Court Title 11 Court Visitor.

Nicole values the fact she is an advocate, guide, and support system for her clients with a focus on solutions.

attorneys.practice_type: Probate and Trust Administration Lawyers in Kent, WA
attorneys.bio:
Patrick’s practice focuses on matters related to Probate/Estate Planning, Business, and related transactions and litigation. Patrick has significant negotiation, trial, mediation and arbitration experience, including jury and non-jury trials. Patrick is practical in his approach and works diligently to obtain positive outcomes for his clients. Patrick provides his clients with confidence that they are being well represented and helps them understand the various options they have so that the best decisions can be made.

During law school, Patrick clerked for the Washington State Attorney General’s Office. After graduating from law school, Patrick was an Associate Attorney with the former law firm of Hanis & Olson. In 2003, he became the first associate to join what has become Hanis Irvine Prothero, PLLC, where he is now a Partner.

Patrick has served as a Commissioner for King County Water District #111 since February 2004, which serves the areas of Meridian Valley and Lake Meridian in Kent, where he lives with his wife Sarah and their five children.

Patrick enjoys devoting his free time to a variety of charitable and community causes, including the Boy Scouts of America, and Kiwanis Children's Cancer Program. Among other organizations, he served as former President of the South King County Bar Association and past President of the Meridian-Kent Kiwanis club.

attorneys.name: Michael M. Hanis
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Kent, WA
attorneys.bio:
Michael M. Hanis is the attorney who conceived the idea of a large and comprehensive law firm in South King County and commenced the initial steps to form the law firm that has become Hanis Irvine Prothero, PLLC.

Mike’s practice is focused on helping people achieve the greatest benefit and protection in their real estate, construction and commercial transactions. Mike was born and raised in South King County, graduating from Renton High School. His deep roots in the community are often a benefit to his clients.

Mike has extensive courtroom experience at every level of the litigation process, including several Washington State Superior Courts, the Washington Court of Appeals, and the Washington State Supreme Court; and before the Federal Courts, including the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. He has negotiated long term water contracts on behalf of agencies providing water service to hundreds of thousands of Puget Sound residents. On behalf of clients he has also, on numerous occasions, appeared before city councils, county councils, and committees of the Washington State Legislature.

Mike is a member of the Washington State Bar Association, the American Bar Association, and other organizations relating to construction and municipal law.

In their free time, Mike and his wife, Peggy, remain committed to the South King County area, where they have spent their entire lives. They are active in community affairs and have participated in Cub Scouts, Youth Soccer, local PTA, Planning Commissions, and community associations. They enjoy boating, traveling, and playing golf. Mike’s other hobbies include photography, motorcycling, and fishing. Mike and his wife also spend much of their free time with their extensive family, which includes four sons and many grandchildren, all of whom make their homes in South King County.

attorneys.name: Sally W. Harmeling
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Wenatchee, WA
attorneys.bio:
Licensed in Washington and Oregon

Sally is a hard worker and an aggressive litigator and advisor.

With more than 15 years experience, Sally litigates civil and commercial disputes, including acting as lead litigator on multi- and single-party matters. Sally handles all aspects of litigation, including pre-litigation negotiations and preparations, lawsuit initiation, discovery and depositions, dispositive motions, trial, and appellate work. Sally is experienced in alternative dispute resolution, including mediation and arbitration.

In addition, Sally practices employment and intellectual property law, both as a litigator and an advisor. She assists clients in selecting, protecting, and policing their intellectual property rights, including prosecuting trademark applications in front of the United States Patent and Trademark Office and litigating trademark infringement. Sally is experienced in protecting certification marks, and acts as outside general counsel for a large gluten-free certification organization. Sally is a former member of the Executive Committee of the Washington State Bar Association's Intellectual Property Section.

Sally grew up in Pacific, Washington, and attended Gonzaga University in Spokane, Washington, where she graduated cum laude. Sally later graduated magna cum laude from the University of San Francisco School of Law. Sally practiced law at Drinker Biddle & Reath LLP, an AmLaw 100 Firm in San Francisco, before moving to Wenatchee and joining JDSA.

Sally currently serves as the Vice President of the Board of Directors for Wenatchee's Numerica Performing Arts Center. She previously served as President of the Chelan-Douglas Counties Bar Association, and on the Boards of Directors of the Chelan Douglas County Volunteer Attorney Services, for Stage Kids (a non-profit children’s musical theater program), and her local homeowners' association, and was a member of the Wenatchee Valley Follies Guild and Children's Foundation.

Sally also teaches spin classes at Sweat Equity Cycle Studio in Wenatchee.

In her free time, Sally enjoys spending time with her husband Ben (a local veterinarian) and their three children, running, traveling, baking, singing, and local community performing arts.

Not only am I a born-and-raised Seattleite, my family traces their Pacific Northwest heritage back to the late 1800s. My grandfather became a lawyer after being a pilot in WWII, my father followed in his footsteps thirty years later, and thirty years after that I added to the family tradition. Clearly, advocating for clients and Northwestern pride runs in my blood.

I have an English degree from the University of Washington, and received my law degree from Seattle University. Since passing the Bar, I have worked exclusively in personal injury practice helping clients recover from both physically and financial from harm. Getting insurance companies to do the right thing and take my clients seriously is a passion for me.

When not at work, or caring for my three beautiful children, I have more passions than I have time for: classic cars, small boat sailing, martial arts, gardening, low-brow sci-fi novels, video games... the list goes on.

attorneys.name: Kevin M. Hastings
attorneys.practice_type: Government Liability Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Kevin Hastings is a tenacious and talented attorney who has dedicated his life to helping those injured by the wrongful acts of others. A northwest native, Kevin comes from a family of commercial fisherman and was inspired to become a lawyer when his uncle suffered catastrophic injury while fishing in the Bering Sea. His uncle's injury has shaped many aspects of Kevin's life, but most importantly, it motivates him to fight tirelessly for his clients.

Kevin welcomes cases with the highest stakes and longest odds, and focuses his practice on personal injury, group home sexual abuse, government liability, wrongful death, class actions, bad faith insurance law, and civil rights. His work tremendously impacts the lives of his clients and their families, and his efforts can be the difference between a client obtaining the means for proper long-term medical support versus filing for bankruptcy due to overwhelming medical bills.

Being the first in his family to graduate college took a lot of grit. While earning tuition money by fishing and other work, Kevin always knew that law was his calling. It was a passion that never let up – he is relentless, determined and thorough, earning the admiration of his colleagues. He respects and appreciates each client’s story and their unique situation, an approach that makes him a better advocate on their behalf.

Kevin began his legal career as a judicial law clerk for Judge C.C. Bridgewater and Judge Jill Johanson at the Washington State Court of Appeals, Division II. Through his work at the court, Kevin gained insight into the judicial process and honed his lawyering skills. After his two-year clerkship, Kevin joined PCVA to fight for clients and pursue justice on their behalf.

In his spare time, Kevin enjoys skiing, snowboarding, hunting, fishing, hiking, cooking, and most of all spending time with his family.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Seattle, WA
attorneys.bio:
Afton hails from Alaska, but she opted to move to Seattle for a proper latte and to attend UW. Graduating with a degree in International Studies, Afton then moved to San Diego to attend law school, graduating in 2006, and later to Los Angeles, where she worked in music law while also raising her young son, which in itself is a kind of “entertainment law”.

Afton returned to Seattle to pursue family law and probate, hoping that her experiences and skills could help others in practical problem-solving. Few attorneys are as attentive to their clients as Afton is to hers.

And that is one of the central values that Afton brings – no nonsense, practical problem-solving skills geared to help clients navigate a very difficult road as smoothly as possible. There are few - if any - areas of family law that Afton cannot provide thoughtful and practical guidance, coupled with strong advocacy. She handles a wide range of divorce cases involving contested custody matters, including international custody cases, and asset division. She also has years of experience drafting both prenuptial and postnuptial agreements. These skills also translate to probate work, which Afton also practices.

There are few - if any - areas of family law that Afton cannot provide thoughtful and practical guidance, coupled with strong advocacy. She handles a wide range of divorce cases involving contested custody matters, including international custody cases, and asset division. She also has years of experience drafting both prenuptial and postnuptial agreements. These skills also translate to probate work, which Afton also practices.
